text:
sasha: Quick RFC follow-up — I dug into the perf delta for different QKV layouts on Ampere/Blackwell. Wanted to capture notes and next steps here.

raj: Nice. TL;DR / what did you find?

sasha: Short: memory-coalescing dominates for shorter sequences. Packing QKV contiguous along feature dim (i.e., last dim) gives much fewer global loads for fused kernels, but kills reuse for kernels that expect separate q,k,v planes. For long sequences, interleaved planar layouts can let us amortize KV cache writes.

emma: Can you show a small example of what you mean by "packed" vs "planar"?

sasha: Sure — pseudo-tensor views:
```
# shapes assume batch B, seq N, heads H, head_dim D
# packed (interleaved QKV): x.view(B, N, H, 3, D).permute(0,1,3,2,4)  # -> B,N,3,H,D contiguous on D
# planar (separate Q/K/V): q = x_q.view(B,N,H,D); k = x_k.view(B,N,H,D); v = x_v.view(B,N,H,D)
```
Packed keeps the inner-most stride across D small and sequential, which is great for vector loads in custom CUDA kernels and for cuBLAS when we fuse GEMM+reorder. Planar gives simpler pointers for KV cache but may cause strided reads when we build fused kernels.

marco: Do we have numbers? microbench?

sasha: Ran quick microbench on g5x (A10G) and b100-equivalent sim:
- seq=32, heads=16, head_dim=64: packed ~1.22x throughput vs planar for our fused mha kernel.
- seq=1024, same config: planar ~1.15x if we rely on blocked matmul + streaming KV writes.
- memory-bound profiles show ~30%-40% lower global load volume for packed at short seq.

liz: Interesting. So layout choice should be sequence-length / workload dependent. That matches theory. But kernels are higher complexity if we support both.

raj: Right. Kernel implications:
- Packed QKV simplifies load patterns for per-token attention (latency optimized) fused kernels.
- Planar allows simpler pointer arithmetic for KV cache (less reshapes at commit time).
- Strided accesses kill L2 / coalescing and increase bank conflicts on shared memory.
- Mixed precision + quantization also interacts: tightly packed int8/4bit needs aligned strides.

emma: Thoughts on API / config surface? We can't force customers to re-lay out their model parameters. Maybe runtime provides a layout abstraction and an automatic rewriter that converts model weights at load time?

marco: +1 for runtime translation. Two possibilities:
1) On-load transform: convert to runtime-favored layout and keep canonical tensors in the model bundle. Pros: single kernel fast path. Cons: storage and one-time CPU/GPU cost.
2) Dual-kernel support: keep both kernels and select at runtime by sequence length / config. Pros: no model rewrite. Cons: maintenance + larger binary.

sasha: I'm leaning towards (1) with a compatibility shim for on-the-fly fallback. Practical reasons: our model onboarding pipeline already rewrites quantization and fused operators. Also simplifies rollout.

liz: How about KV cache layout for streaming/serving? If we rewrite weights to packed, then KV cache will also be packed — which hurts append/streaming semantics unless we maintain per-head pointers.

raj: Implementation idea: store KV cache as planar in device memory but expose a tiny indirection layer to the kernel that maps planar -> packed view without copies when possible. For append we can write into planar buffer and have the kernel scatter-gather into packed tile-views. That avoids rewriting every step.

emma: That indirection sounds complex. Any alternatives? Using a cooperative copy kernel that converts newly appended rows into packed tiles asynchronously?

sasha: Yes — background writer approach works: append to planar ring buffer, then a CUDA kernel converts new rows into packed tiles in L2-friendly chunks. The fused MHA consumes packed tiles. Latency impact is bounded by pipeline depth.

marco: We should measure conversion overhead vs end-to-end latency for streaming workloads (single-token step). If conversion takes >0.5ms that's a problem for low-latency apps.

liz: Also important: provide a config flag for customers who want strict determinism / no on-the-fly transforms. Documented fallback to planar only kernels.

infra-bot: perf-bench queued: run_attention_bench --layout {packed,planar} --seq 8,32,128,512,1024 --heads 8,16 --head-dim 32,64 --batch 1,8 --runs 100

raj: Good. Bench plan: measure throughput, p50 latency, p99 latency, GPU memory bandwidth, cupti sm_eff, l2_hit_rate. Use perf profiling for a subset.

sasha: Action items:
- sasha: add small perf harness to attention repo that can run above bench (ETA 2d)
- marco: prototype on-load layout rewriter for model bundles (ETA 1 week)
- emma: design runtime layout abstraction API + config flags doc (ETA 3d)
- raj: prepare perf scripts and config for perf infra (ETA 2d)
- liz: write note for SDK compatibility and determinism opt-out (ETA 3d)

emma: Can we target a soft rollout: default to on-load rewrite for hosted models, opt-in for dedicated/private until proven?

sasha: Yeah that's the plan. Hosted => rewrite by default, with toggle. Dedicated/private get opt-in until we ship quantization + eval regressions check.

marco: One more nit: watch out for padding / alignment. For head_dim not divisible by 32 we may need trailing padding to keep coalesced accesses. This affects memory footprint and KV cache sizing. Add pad policy to rewriter.

sasha: Noted. I'll include pad strategy in the rewriter PR.

liz: Thanks — this clarifies tradeoffs. Keep thread updated with bench links. :thumbsup:

raj: Thanks all, moving perf jobs into queue.
